newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ says Tehran recalls envoy, doubts trade ban.
newsitem.headline: NZ says Tehran recalls envoy, doubts trade ban.

text.p: New Zealand Trade Minister Lockwood Smith said on Monday that Iran was recalling its ambassador to Wellington in the diplomatic aftermath of a German court ruling that Tehran had ordered political killings.
"Their ambassador is also being recalled," he told a news conference.
He added that Wellington had still not received any confirmation of a reported Iranian ban on trade with New Zealand.
"There has been no official confirmation from Iran... there could have been some misunderstanding of this," he said.

New Zealand recalled its ambassador Daniel Richards for consultations last Friday as part of an international move led by Europe after a German court ruled Iran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Richards is expected to go back to the Middle Eastern country by the end of the week, Smith said.
The minister added there had been no Iranian indication of how long Tehran would keep its ambassador there, "but I imagine it is for consultations, just like ours".
One potential benefit of the Iranian envoy returning home was that he would be able to clarify any confusion about the context of New Zealand's move, Smith noted.
He said that one possible reason for the reported trade ban might have been that an early report of Wellington's action on Friday suggested New Zealand planned to cut trade ties.
"He (the ambassador) knows New Zealand is not planning any trade embargoes," Smith added.
Above all, the minister said New Zealand wanted to repair relations with Iran.
"We have always had good relations with Iran and we want to get them back on a good footing," he said.
